correction_notes: Initial graph build (not a correction pass). Evidence uses paraphrase-anchored tags (E<n>) keyed to paper sections/paragraphs, since no sentence-indexed source was provided. Edges reflect explicit causal/support language in the text (e.g., 'because', 'this suggests', ablation deltas); coordinate/parallel statements joined by 'and' without dependency language are left as separate isolated nodes rather than force-linked.

nodes.name: Encoder-decoder decoupling
nodes.description: LaMaTE decouples encoding and decoding from language modeling by using an LLM as the NMT encoder and leaving the NMT decoder unchanged.

nodes.name: Modeling flexibility
nodes.description: Decoupling encoding and decoding confers modeling flexibility, allowing a deep complex encoder paired with a lightweight decoder.

nodes.name: Heterogeneous architecture suitability
nodes.description: The heterogeneous architecture (powerful encoder, lightweight decoder) is well-suited for MT, using a powerful encoder to understand input while generating translations at lower decoding cost.

nodes.name: Inference speedup result
nodes.description: LaMaTE achieves 2.4-6.5x inference speedups over baselines.

nodes.name: KV cache memory reduction result
nodes.description: LaMaTE achieves a 75% reduction in KV cache memory footprint.

nodes.name: LLM decoder as unidirectional encoder
nodes.description: The function Dec_theta( , [c,x]) serves as a unidirectional encoder in LaMaTE.

nodes.name: Whole model as hybrid LM
nodes.description: Because both the LaMaTE encoder and decoder are unidirectional, the whole model can roughly be thought of as a hybrid language model: a large model for prefilling, a small model for decoding.

nodes.name: Dimensionality mismatch problem
nodes.description: The LLM decoder may have a larger hidden size than the NMT decoder, creating a mismatch.

nodes.name: Adaptor introduced
nodes.description: An adaptor is added to the output of the LLM decoder to reduce its dimensionality to match the NMT decoder.

nodes.name: Plain linear adaptor insufficient
nodes.description: A simple linear mapping adaptor falls short because LLMs are too big, making it difficult for untrained smaller models to use the transformed representations directly.

nodes.name: Three-component adaptor design
nodes.description: An adaptor with three components (layer fusion, MLP, EncStack) is designed to make better use of LLM outputs for the NMT decoder.

nodes.name: Layer fusion mechanism
nodes.description: LLM layers are divided into K groups and their outputs fused via a learnable weighted sum plus layer norm (Hfuse).

nodes.name: Layer fusion motivation
nodes.description: Fusing outputs of intermediate layers (rather than only the final layer) forms a finer-grained output, a method found beneficial to deep-to-shallow architectures in prior NMT work.

nodes.name: MLP dimensionality reduction
nodes.description: A 2-layer MLP is placed after layer fusion to reduce hidden size from d1 to d2, matching the NMT decoder's hidden size.

nodes.name: EncStack bidirectional learning
nodes.description: A stack of Transformer encoder layers (EncStack) is used to learn bidirectional representations from the unidirectional adaptor output, added with small computational overhead.

nodes.name: Ablation: no layer fusion
nodes.description: Removing layer fusion causes a COMET drop of 0.24 and BLEU drop of 0.71 relative to full LaMaTE.

nodes.name: Ablation: no EncStack
nodes.description: Removing EncStack causes a COMET drop of 0.30 and BLEU drop of 0.53 relative to full LaMaTE.

nodes.name: Layer fusion informativeness conclusion
nodes.description: Fusing intermediate LLM layers provides a more informative representation than relying solely on the final layer.

nodes.name: Adaptor enhances LLM representations conclusion
nodes.description: The adaptor enhances the native representations of LLMs, rendering them more suitable for the NMT decoder.

flagged_edges: P18,P19 left unconnected to other nodes within component: parallel adaptor sub-components with no stated dependency ordering

nodes.name: Fine-tuning LLMs is costly
nodes.description: Fine-tuning pre-trained LLMs is costly, making it generally favorable to use less labeled data.

nodes.name: Less data causes inadequate learning
nodes.description: Using less labeled data can lead to inadequate learning of the new parameters (adaptor and NMT decoder).

nodes.name: Extensive fine-tuning causes forgetting
nodes.description: Extensive fine-tuning may cause the LLM to forget its original knowledge encoded in its parameters.

nodes.name: Two-stage training method introduced
nodes.description: A two-stage training method is presented to perform more efficient learning for different types of parameters.

nodes.name: Stage 1: frozen LLM pretraining
nodes.description: In stage 1, the LLM decoder is frozen while the adaptor and NMT decoder are pre-trained on a standard translation task.

nodes.name: Stage 1 avoids backward pass
nodes.description: Because the LLM decoder parameters are frozen in stage 1, only a forward pass through the large network is needed, avoiding the backward pass.

nodes.name: Stage 1 is less computationally expensive
nodes.description: Avoiding the backward pass through the LLM makes stage 1 less computationally expensive than full LLM fine-tuning, enabling scaling to large datasets.

nodes.name: Stage 2: joint fine-tuning
nodes.description: In stage 2, the LLM decoder, NMT decoder, and adaptor are fine-tuned together on various tasks using the ComMT dataset.

nodes.name: Ablation: without stage 2
nodes.description: Training with only stage 1 (W/o S2) results in a substantial performance drop (COMET -2.25, BLEU -4.18).

nodes.name: Ablation: stage 2 with frozen LLM
nodes.description: Incorporating stage 2 while freezing LLM parameters yields improvements over stage-1-only but still falls short of full LaMaTE performance (COMET -0.16, BLEU -0.12).

nodes.name: Both data and LLM tuning matter conclusion
nodes.description: The ablation results underscore the importance of both high-quality data and LLM parameter tuning in maximizing model performance.

nodes.name: Gap in universal translation data resources
nodes.description: There remains a notable gap in comprehensive, high-quality data resources tailored to developing universal translation models.

nodes.name: ComMT benchmark developed
nodes.description: ComMT, a new comprehensive evaluation/training benchmark spanning five diverse translation-related tasks, is developed to generalize and evaluate LaMaTE.

nodes.name: ComMT task set
nodes.description: ComMT comprises five tasks: General Translation, Document-level Translation, Domain Translation, Terminology-constrained Translation, and Automatic Post-editing.

nodes.name: ComMT training set size
nodes.description: ComMT's training set totals 239,661 samples across four languages (German, Czech, Russian, Chinese).

nodes.name: ComMT quality verification setup
nodes.description: Llama3-8B was fine-tuned on ComMT and compared against WMT17-20 and TowerBlock datasets, evaluated on the WMT23 test set.

nodes.name: ComMT outperforms WMT17-20
nodes.description: ComMT surpasses WMT17-WMT20 in both En->X and X->En directions.

nodes.name: ComMT underperforms TowerBlock on X->En
nodes.description: ComMT excels in En->X but underperforms TowerBlock in the X->En direction.

nodes.name: TowerBlock size/composition explanation
nodes.description: The X->En discrepancy versus TowerBlock may be attributed to TowerBlock's larger dataset size and its inclusion of additional general task data predominantly in English.

nodes.name: LaMaTE vs encoder-decoder baselines
nodes.description: LaMaTE surpasses NLLB-3.3B, NMT, and mT5-Large across all evaluated ComMT tasks.

nodes.name: LLMs as high-capacity encoders conclusion
nodes.description: This result highlights the potential of LLMs as high-capacity encoders, capable of producing more expressive and informative representations.

nodes.name: Better representations improve decoder foundation
nodes.description: The enhanced representations from LLM encoding provide a solid foundation for the decoder, ultimately improving translation quality.

nodes.name: LaMaTE comparable to Llama3-8B-SFT
nodes.description: LaMaTE achieves comparable overall performance to Llama3-8B-SFT, a fully fine-tuned decoder-only LLM.

nodes.name: LLMs as effective MT encoders conclusion
nodes.description: The comparability to Llama3-8B-SFT demonstrates that LLMs can serve as effective MT encoders, offering an efficient alternative to fine-tuning LLMs as direct generators.

nodes.name: Encoder-decoder models show lower misalignment
nodes.description: Encoder-decoder models (mT5-large, LaMaTE) consistently exhibit lower off-target rate, unaligned source words, and unaligned target words than decoder-only models.

nodes.name: LaMaTE mitigates misalignment
nodes.description: LaMaTE follows the encoder-decoder paradigm, which also helps mitigate misalignment issues as an added bonus.

nodes.name: Cross-attention hypothesis
nodes.description: The misalignment improvement is speculated to be attributable to the cross-attention mechanism in the NMT decoder, which allows direct token-wise interaction between target and source.

nodes.name: Cross-attention enhances alignment
nodes.description: Cross-attention enhances source-target alignment, in contrast to LLMs relying on a single attention mechanism over concatenated source and target text.

nodes.name: Single attention causes lost focus
nodes.description: Relying on a single attention mechanism to jointly process concatenated source and target text could potentially cause a loss of attention focus.

flagged_edges: P60->P58 direction inferred: text presents cross-attention hypothesis first, then contrasts with single-attention/lost-focus explanation for decoder-only models; causal ordering between P58 and P60 is not fully explicit

nodes.name: Ablation: Concat Decoder variant
nodes.description: The Concat Decoder variant, which removes cross-attention, underperforms the standard decoder (COMET -0.80, BLEU -2.34).

nodes.name: Ablation: Prefix Decoder variant
nodes.description: The Prefix Decoder variant, which also removes cross-attention, underperforms the standard decoder (COMET -0.66, BLEU -1.47).

nodes.name: Standard decoder superiority conclusion
nodes.description: The standard decoder proves superior to the alternative cross-attention-free decoder designs.

nodes.name: Cross-attention beneficial for alignment-demanding tasks
nodes.description: Together with the misalignment findings, maintaining cross-attention in the decoder is argued to be particularly beneficial for translation tasks that demand strong alignment.

nodes.name: Decoder depth increases quality but reduces speed
nodes.description: Increasing decoder layers significantly improves translation performance, particularly En->X, but decoding speed drops sharply as depth increases, with a 39% reduction from 8 to 16 layers.

nodes.name: Encoder scaling offers better trade-off conclusion
nodes.description: Because decoder depth improves quality but sharply hurts speed while EncStack depth gives only modest gains with minimal efficiency cost, scaling the encoder offers a more effective trade-off between performance and computational efficiency than scaling the decoder.

nodes.name: EncStack depth gives modest gains
nodes.description: Adding more EncStack layers leads to modest improvements in both translation directions, with relatively small gains compared to decoder variations.

nodes.name: EncStack depth has minimal efficiency impact
nodes.description: Since EncStack operates only on the encoder side, its impact on decoding efficiency is minimal.

nodes.name: LaMaTE underperforms on low-resource languages
nodes.description: LaMaTE underperforms compared to mT5-large in low- and very-low-resource languages in the large-scale 99-language evaluation.

nodes.name: Limited pretraining data explanation
nodes.description: The low-resource underperformance is likely due to limited pre-training data for these languages in the Llama3-base model.

nodes.name: Stronger multilingual encoder suggestion
nodes.description: Using a model with stronger multilingual capabilities as the encoder could further improve performance on low-resource languages.

nodes.name: Decoder lightweight design
nodes.description: The NMT decoder in LaMaTE is intentionally lightweight relative to the LLM encoder.

nodes.name: Lightweight decoder may bottleneck many-target-language generation
nodes.description: Because the decoder is lightweight, it may become a bottleneck when generating translations into many target languages.

nodes.name: Expanding decoder capacity essential
nodes.description: Expanding decoder capacity is essential for better performance given this potential bottleneck.

nodes.name: MoE scaling suggestion
nodes.description: A more effective strategy might involve scaling the decoder's capacity with Mixture-of-Experts instead of adding more layers, boosting performance without compromising efficiency.

nodes.name: Randomly initialized decoder requires stage-1 pretraining
nodes.description: The approach requires pre-training the decoder's parameters using large-scale bilingual data in stage 1 because the decoder is randomly initialized.

nodes.name: Stage-1 pretraining may be inefficient
nodes.description: The requirement to pre-train a randomly initialized decoder on large-scale bilingual data may not be the most efficient process.

nodes.name: Alternative initialization suggestion
nodes.description: Future work could explore initializing decoder parameters from the encoder or leveraging a small pre-trained language model to reduce the state gap between encoder and decoder.

nodes.name: Llama3-8B best multilingual backbone
nodes.description: Llama3-8B consistently outperformed XGLM-7.5B, Bloom-7B, Falcon-7B, and Qwen2-7B in 0-shot and 3-shot translation across En<->De/Cs/Ru/Zh.

nodes.name: Stronger multilingual capability inference
nodes.description: Llama3-8B's superior cross-lingual performance suggests it possesses stronger multilingual capabilities.

nodes.name: Llama3-8B selected as backbone
nodes.description: Based on the evaluation results, Llama3-8B was selected as the backbone model for subsequent LaMaTE experiments.

isolated_nodes.name: NLP focus on decoder-only models
isolated_nodes.description: Much recent NLP emphasis has been on modeling MT and other problems using a single pre-trained Transformer decoder.

isolated_nodes.name: Encoder-decoder architectures receive less attention
isolated_nodes.description: Encoder-decoder architectures, standard in earlier NMT models, have received relatively less attention.

isolated_nodes.name: LLMs computationally expensive
isolated_nodes.description: LLMs are computationally expensive and pose challenges for applications requiring low latency and small memory footprint.

isolated_nodes.name: Analyze-then-generate paradigm
isolated_nodes.description: Most MT models, traditional and LLM-based, operate on an analyze-then-generate paradigm.

isolated_nodes.name: BERT-style encoder pretraining
isolated_nodes.description: A large body of NLP work has focused on pretraining and applying text encoders such as BERT for language understanding.

isolated_nodes.name: LLMs as text encoders for embeddings
isolated_nodes.description: Recent work has fine-tuned LLMs for text encoding and shown they can produce high-quality representations for embedding tasks.

isolated_nodes.name: Rarity of LLM encoders for generation
isolated_nodes.description: It is rare to see studies incorporating LLMs in the encoding side for NMT or other language generation tasks.

isolated_nodes.name: MT research shift to LLM adaptation
isolated_nodes.description: The focus of MT research has shifted toward adapting LLMs (prompting, fine-tuning) rather than improving model architectures.

isolated_nodes.name: Complementarity with efficiency methods
isolated_nodes.description: Quantization, pruning, and speculative decoding methods are not contradictory with LaMaTE and can be combined with it.

isolated_nodes.name: Two-stage architecture as hybrid LM framing
isolated_nodes.description: The whole LaMaTE system can be viewed as a single language model since both encoder and decoder are language-model-based.

isolated_nodes.name: Prompt-guided task control
isolated_nodes.description: By giving an appropriate prompt, the system can be guided to produce outputs following specific needs or contexts, giving LaMaTE an advantage over traditional NMT models.

isolated_nodes.name: ComMT collection goals
isolated_nodes.description: ComMT data was collected with two goals: maximizing data source diversity and maximizing high-quality manually annotated data.

isolated_nodes.name: ComMT covers four languages
isolated_nodes.description: ComMT is multilingual and supports four languages: German, Czech, Russian, and Chinese.

isolated_nodes.name: Original source language requirement
isolated_nodes.description: The test set ensures the source language is original in each case to avoid translationese issues.

isolated_nodes.name: Some languages lack test sets
isolated_nodes.description: Some languages currently lack test sets in ComMT because obtaining task data is challenging.

isolated_nodes.name: Efficient methods compatibility
isolated_nodes.description: Since LaMaTE follows standard encoding/decoding, it can be easily combined with various efficient inference methods.

structural_reasoning: The graph captures LaMaTE's main argumentative chains: architecture motivation -> speed/memory results (C1); the LLM-decoder-as-encoder framing and adaptor necessity (C2); the three-part adaptor design and its ablations (C3); the two-stage training rationale and its ablations (C4); the ComMT benchmark motivation and quality-verification results (C5); main results and the 'LLMs as encoders' interpretive claims (C6); misalignment analysis with a speculative causal mechanism (C7, lower confidence since the causal direction between cross-attention and single-attention explanations is somewhat inferred); decoder-variant ablations reinforcing the cross-attention claim (C8); depth-vs-efficiency trade-off reasoning (C9); low-resource underperformance diagnosis (C10); and two limitations chains (C11 decoder bottleneck, C12 stage-1 initialization cost). Background/related-work statements and standalone descriptive facts (dataset composition, prior-work framing) are left as isolated nodes since the text does not present them as premises feeding a specific downstream claim. Confidence is single_run throughout since only one extraction pass was performed (no multi-run voting), which caps edge_score below the DecomposeRL reference graph's unanimous-vote components.
